thread:
incident-bot: 🔔 INCIDENT detected: kv-cache-pressure-high on cluster-prod-7. Metric: p99/generation_latency = 3.6s (SLO 2s). Streaming stalls observed. Alert group: storage/kv/shard-pressure. severity=P1
Alex: Saw it. p95 also creeping up — ~420ms now. Streaming tail shows repeated stalls. Confirming impact surface: hosted API gen + streaming.
Priya: I can repro a tail stall in staging with a long context (>8k). Logs show heavy eviction and lots of prefill ops queued.
Sam: Adding initial blast: # of streams with stalls >5s jumped 10x in last 6m.
Jorge: Key hypothesis: slab fragmentation + prefill vs decode scheduling imbalance. Prefill tasks are saturating decode threads leading to queueing.
Maya: Any automated mitigations we can flip quickly?
Alex: Rolling immediate mitigations: 1) lower prefill task priority 2) increase target slab size for hot set 3) enable temporary shard throttle to shed bursts. I'll run commands.
Alex: Running: 
```
# increase eviction aggressiveness
kubectl -n infra exec kv-shard-7 -- redis-cli CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy volatile-lru
# bump slab allocation (temporary)
curl -X POST https://control-plane/internal/kv/shard/7/sizes -d '{"target_mb": 12288}'
```
Priya: Copy. While Alex runs that, I'm going to temporarily route streaming traffic to fallback-infer (lower-cost, slightly older model) to preserve latency for customers.
Priya: `deploy-bot: deploy fallback-infer v0.9 -> prod routing 10%`
deploy-bot: @Priya started rollout: fallback-infer v0.9 at 10% traffic. Canary OK so far.
Sam: Observability: p95 drops from 420ms -> 330ms after throttle. p99 still at ~2.8s, but trending down. Streaming stalls reduced by ~40%.
Jorge: I dug into allocator logs — fragmentation spikes at ~10:12:03 UTC, correlates with a large batch of prefill requests from a single tenant. Prefill queue length hit 4k.
Maya: Can we blacklist that tenant temporarily or throttle at ingress?
Alex: Temporarily applied per-tenant rate limit to tenant-t-834: `rate-limit set tenant-t-834 20r/min`
Priya: Noted. Also switching prefill worker pool to background QoS: `prefill.scheduler=background` — applies to cluster-prod-7.
Sam: After changes: p95 ~310ms, p99 1.9s (just under SLO). Streaming stalls count down to ~2x baseline. Good progress.
Alex: Root-cause summary draft: slab fragmentation + imbalanced scheduling where prefill tasks consumed decode resources, leading to long tail stalls on streaming paths. Large single-tenant burst amplified the fragmentation.
Jorge: Long-term actions (tickets): - add shard-level prefill throttles - implement allocator compaction on low-traffic windows - expose prefill/decoder queue metrics for alerting - improve per-tenant backpressure
Maya: Customer impact: small subset of streaming requests hit p99 > 2s for ~12m. No data loss, responses eventually served. We should prepare a short note for CS: impacted customers may have seen slow streaming and higher latencies.
Priya: I'll draft a blameless post with timeline + mitigation commands + next steps. Will include the tenant burst ID + request samples.
Alex: Handoff: I'm going offline in 20m. Maya, can you take primary oncall for the remainder and watch p99 for the next 2hrs? I'll leave the rollback knobs I used in the runbook.
Maya: Taking over. Watching dashboards (p95/p99 + streaming stalls + prefill queue). I've got the mitigation toggles: revert prefill.scheduler, adjust slab target, tenant rate-limits, and rollback routing.
Jorge: Leaving a tip: when fragmentation recurs, run compaction job: `infra-tool compaction run --shard 7 --mode aggressive` (night windows preferred).
Sam: I've exported traces for 10 slow streams and attached links to the thread (internal tracer links).
deploy-bot: rollout progress: fallback-infer v0.9 at 10% -> 30% stable.
Priya: CS note draft: "We observed increased gen/streaming latency affecting a subset of requests for ~12 minutes due to KV cache pressure; mitigations applied and performance restored to within SLO. No customer data was lost. Engineering taking steps to prevent recurrence."
Alex: Saved. Also creating follow-up tickets for infra/sre and runtime: SRE-2247 (prefill throttles), RUNTIME-881 (allocator compaction), PLAT-640 (prefill-vs-decode fairness).
Maya: Confirming observability alerts adjusted and we'll alert on prefill queue >1000 as a new signal.
Alex: Final check: p99 stable at 1.7s, streaming stalls ~baseline. I'm handing off fully to Maya. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
Maya: Acknowledged. I'll escalate if anything regresses. Adding timeline + commands to the incident doc.
incident-bot: INCIDENT update: severity-> mitigated. Duration: 00:18:25. links: internal/ops/incidents/1799005555.
Priya: Postmortem scheduled: 1hr postmortem sync at 11:45 UTC. Invite: infra, runtime, devex, cs.
Alex: Logged. Good job everyone.
Maya: Closing thread here, will update incident doc with copies of the commands and tenant id.
